finding.claim: A public key without PEM armor is treated as an HMAC secret when algorithms is unset or includes HS*, enabling algorithm confusion: an attacker who knows the public key can forge HS256 tokens.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled token; the verifier key is public material with no PEM header.
finding.sink: verifySignature HS branch (src/crypto.js:396-398) accepts an HMAC keyed with the public key text.

trace.note: String key passes option validation.
detectPublicKeyAlgorithms(key, []) is called; empty providedAlgorithms skips the HS shortcut.
locatePem finds no uppercase -----BEGIN header and returns isRawSecret=true.
assertNotAsymmetricJwkJson only inspects JSON; the key is not JSON, so it passes.
Raw secret branch returns hsAlgorithms.
allowedAlgorithms is set to hsAlgorithms.
prepareKeyOrSecret(key, true) yields a secret KeyObject.
Attacker HS256 token is verified against the public key bytes and accepted.

finding.guards_checked: PEM header matcher requires an uppercase BEGIN header (crypto.js:40, 131-133); JWK guard only blocks JSON (crypto.js:100-122, 143-147); algorithms allowlist (verifier.js:170) protects only when restricted to asymmetric algorithms; RS/HS cross-check (verifier.js:550-556) does not apply because no asymmetric algorithm is detected.

finding.claim: Claim validators (aud, iss, sub, jti, nonce, exp, maxAge/iat) are skipped when the claim is absent, so a validly signed token missing the claim is accepted unless requiredClaims lists it.
finding.source: Validly signed token (same key) whose payload omits aud, iss, exp, or iat.

trace.note: verify sync path calls verifyToken.
Signature verified successfully.
requiredClaims check runs only if the option is set; it is off by default.
Validator loop: if claim is absent, continue skips the check.
Token accepted and cached.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first (verifier.js:288); type checks and crit validation run after signature; requiredClaims is opt-in (verifier.js:301-307); signer noTimestamp (signer.js:129) yields tokens with no iat, so maxAge is never enforced for them.

finding.claim: Non-canonical base64url signature encodings are accepted, so a single valid signature corresponds to several distinct token strings. Apps keying revocation or replay caches on the raw token string can be bypassed.
finding.source: A valid issued token; attacker varies unused trailing bits of the final signature character.
finding.sink: Application-level revocation or one-time-use check keyed on the raw token string (library-level signature check still passes).

trace.note: Alphabet-only regex; no length or trailing-bit canonicality check.
Signature segment passes the alphabet check.
Buffer.from(signature,'base64') ignores non-zero unused trailing bits.
timingSafeEqual compares decoded bytes, so the variant verifies.

finding.guards_checked: Base64url alphabet regex (decoder.js:10, 41); HMAC covers the raw signing input (verifier.js:403, 177), so header and payload cannot be altered; only the signature segment is malleable (HS256 gives 4 variants of the last character).

finding.claim: When caching is enabled, a Buffer token causes a TypeError from verify() instead of a TokenError, because the cache key is computed before decoding.
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token (for example req.body) to a verifier created with cache enabled.
finding.sink: Non-TokenError exception thrown synchronously from verify, before the callback in async mode.

trace.note: Buffer tokens are accepted by the type check.
cacheKeyBuilder(token) runs before decode when cache is set.
hashToken calls token.split, which does not exist on Buffer, so a TypeError is thrown.

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:361 admits Buffers; no conversion to string happens before the cache lookup.

finding.claim: In async mode with complete:true, the returned input field is the full token including the signature; sync mode returns the signing input only. Results are inconsistent across modes.
finding.source: Caller using complete:true with the async API.
finding.sink: Consumer code that uses result.input for signing-input processing or re-verification.

trace.note: Sync/async decode produces input as the signing input (token.slice(0, lastSeparator)).
Sync path returns decoded input.
Async path returns input: token (full token).

finding.guards_checked: None relevant; this is a correctness inconsistency, not an authentication bypass.

finding.claim: The caller-supplied header option is spread after alg, so it can override the alg field while the signature is produced with the configured algorithm, creating a header/signature mismatch.
finding.source: Caller-supplied header option (developer-controlled unless the app passes untrusted input).
finding.sink: Emitted token header alg no longer matches the algorithm used to sign.

trace.note: header object built as {alg, typ, kid, ...additionalHeader}.
Signature produced with the configured algorithm, not the header alg.

finding.guards_checked: Option type checks at signer.js:335-337 only verify that header is an object; no alg consistency check.

finding.claim: A payload-supplied iat sets the base for exp and nbf computed from expiresIn/notBefore, so untrusted payload fields can choose token lifetime.
finding.source: Application signs a payload built from untrusted input that includes iat (mass assignment).

trace.note: iat = payload.iat * 1000 || clockTimestamp || Date.now().
exp = iat + expiresIn when expiresIn is set.
nbf = iat + notBefore when notBefore is set.

finding.guards_checked: exp must be a positive integer when present in payload (signer.js:108-110), but the expiresIn-derived exp overrides it; no check on iat origin.
